claim: Foot Locker France headcount, from its statutory equal-pay index posters, fell from 1,669 employees (2024 data, 2025 poster, index 88/100, 46% women) to 1,634 (2025 data, 2026 poster, index 89/100, 44% women), down 35 or 2.1%. The 2026 poster still carries Foot Locker, Inc. branding, not DICK'S.
data_point: Foot Locker France employees 1,669 (CY2024 basis) to 1,634 (CY2025 basis), -2.1%; about 11-12 per store on ~140-149 locator stores
evidence_date: 2026 poster (2025 data; French law requires publication by 1 March 2026); 2025 poster (2024 data)
source_name: Foot Locker France equal-pay index posters 2026 (FR) and 2025 (EN, footlocker-emea.com)
original_quote: Le calcul est basé sur 1 634 employés, dont 44 % de femmes et 56 % d'hommes.
english_translation: The calculation is based on 1,634 employees, 44% women and 56% men.
verifier_note: Both PDFs fetched and read. 2026 FR poster: 'Foot Locker France a obtenu un indice d'egalite de 89 sur 100 pour 2026 (sur la base des donnees de 2025) ... 1 634 employes', header logo 'Foot Locker, Inc.'. 2025 EN poster (https://www.footlocker-emea.com/content/dam/final/footlockereurope/Online_activations/downloads/equal_pay_france_2025/The_Equal_Pay_Index_EN.pdf): 'index for 2025 (based on 2024 data) of 88 out of 100 ... based on 1,669 employees, 46% women and 54% men'. The exact 2026-02-27 publication date was not verified. Downgraded A to B: the index headcount is a calendar-year workforce figure (Egapro method), so CY2025 is mostly pre-deal months and the -2.1% is a weak signal of DKS-era cuts. It does give a France headcount base for sizing redundancy costs. Not in baseline (which has only the 11,100 international total) or in other confirmed files (the BODACC agent's 1,249 headcount is dated 2020).

claim: Paris Bastille store at 12 rue du Faubourg Saint-Antoine (store no. 05923, the former 'Jordan store') closed in summer 2025, around the deal close. In a LinkedIn comment, Foot Locker's VP Real Estate EMEA Pierre Combet said the landlord 'supported us a lot at the end' but the street had 'taken a real beating'. The landlord-side post says an international brand will open in the unit.
data_point: 1 Paris high-street exit, at or just before deal close (Paris city page listed it on 2025-07-13 but not on 2025-09-11); lease exit after landlord rent support
source_name: LinkedIn post by a landlord-side broker, with a comment by Pierre Combet (VP Real Estate EMEA, Foot Locker); FL locator via Wayback
original_quote: Notre ancien Foot Locker (Jordan store à la grande époque)… un bailleur très compréhensif qui nous a beaucoup supporté sur la fin mais une artère parisienne qui a pris une sacrée taule.
english_translation: Our former Foot Locker (the Jordan store in its heyday)... a very understanding landlord who supported us a lot at the end, but a Parisian street that took a real beating.
verifier_note: LinkedIn page fetched: Combet's comment is there essentially verbatim. The post refers to a Faubourg Saint-Antoine facade and says 'Dans quelques mois s'ouvrira le point de vente d'une enseigne internationale', without naming the brand. The activity id decodes to 2025-09-09 05:30 UTC. Combet's title is confirmed in A_w1_company-side-new. The removal timing comes from another agent's Wayback diff (raw/D_w1_locator-census-west.md: on the Paris city page 2025-07-13, gone 2025-09-11); I could not re-fetch Wayback from this session. The store's own page was last captured with HTTP 200 on 2024-11-09. Downgraded B to C: the exit is pre-deal or at the close, so it does not add to the DKS-era closure count. Its value is the real-estate head's description of a negotiated lease exit. The only earlier mention, in D_w1_locator-census-west, is a verifier note that this item was not checked, so it is not a duplicate.

claim: AGAINST: the Reims city-centre store (16 place Myron-Herrick, store no. 05150) was refitted under DKS ownership. Per the local paper it closed on 26 Mar 2026 for works and was due to reopen on 17 Apr 2026. The store shows normal hours on the live locator.
data_point: 1 French high-street store refitted in Q1 FY26 (about 3 weeks closed); SIRENE establishment 38240186700561 active, 10-19 employees
original_quote: Le magasin de chaussures étasunien de la place Myron-Herrick est fermé depuis le 26 mars pour se refaire une beauté. La réouverture est programmée ce vendredi 17 avril
english_translation: The US shoe shop on place Myron-Herrick has been closed since 26 March for a makeover; reopening is set for Friday 17 April.
verifier_note: The article body could not be fetched (WebFetch is blocked for this domain, the Apify quota is exhausted and the session's web-search budget is spent), so the quote is unverified. Corroboration: the Google News RSS result saved in the scraper's scratchpad shows the headline 'Vague de renovations dans de grandes enseignes du centre-ville de Reims - L'Hebdo du Vendredi' dated 14 Apr 2026. FL's locator lists Reims 05150 at 16 Place Myron Herrick as OPEN with Mon-Sat hours (scraper's crawl, 2026-10-07). SIRENE shows the establishment active. Downgraded B to C: the quote is unverified, and it is a single-store refit, likely a low-capex Fast Break-type reset.

claim: Marseille rue Saint-Ferréol: Foot Locker moved from 77-79 rue Saint-Ferréol to a smaller unit at 31 rue Saint-Ferréol on the same street, and JLL marketed the old unit as 'Division de l'ancien Foot Locker'. CORRECTION: the move happened in July 2024, before the deal, not in late 2025 or early 2026; the Feb-2026 article is a look back.
data_point: SIRENE: 77 rue Saint-Ferreol establishment (38240186700496, 20-49 staff) closed 2024-07-20; 31 rue Saint-Ferreol (38240186702112) opened 2024-07-26; locator store 05209 at 31 rue Saint-Ferreol open. The old unit had 240 m2 of sales floor plus 325 m2 of basement (JLL, per the scraper).
source_name: actu Marseille (Fabien Binacchi); INSEE SIRENE; JLL listing
original_quote: certains choisissent aussi de déménager pour plus petit. Le spécialiste de la fripe KiloShop, Foot Locker ou Rituals ont ainsi changé d'adresse tout en restant sur le même axe.
english_translation: Some also choose to move somewhere smaller; thrift specialist KiloShop, Foot Locker and Rituals changed address while staying on the same street.
verifier_note: The actu.fr article and the JLL listing could not be fetched (actu.fr is blocked for WebFetch, JLL returned 403, Apify is out of quota and the search budget is spent), so the quote is unverified. SIRENE data saved by the BODACC agent independently confirms a same-street relocation from no. 77 to no. 31 dated 2024-07-20/26. That makes this a PRE-DEAL downsizing, and it should not be counted as DKS-era rightsizing. The scraper's claim that 'Marseille hyper-centre went from 2 doors to 1 smaller one' mixes this 2024 move with the end-2025 Centre Bourse closure, which is already confirmed elsewhere. The finding is only useful as context on smaller formats.
